answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it earns access to jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. A quill-signed work history can accumulate reputation, while random mirror checks compare claims with completed tasks and a pulse of fresh challenges tests control of the same account. Creating many identities no longer grants free influence: the attacker must fund each stake, keep identities active, and risk losing capital when fabricated histories are exposed.
